passages.title: Loss and the return to Bethlehem
passages.summary: Famine takes Elimelech’s household to Moab. After three deaths, Naomi returns. Ruth stays with her, while Orpah returns home. Naomi and her daughters-in-law face grief and hard choices. Naomi blesses both women before Ruth stays.
passages.uncertainty: The map shows the named town and broad region. It does not identify private buildings or an ancient road.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies Ruth's loyalty and faith during loss.

passages.title: Ruth gleans in Boaz’s field
passages.summary: Ruth gathers leftover grain. Boaz provides protection, food, and additional grain. Naomi recognizes his connection with their family. Gleaning means collecting grain left after harvest. Boaz protects Ruth at work and helps her feed Naomi.
passages.uncertainty: The map shows the named town and broad region. It does not identify private buildings or an ancient road.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies kindness and trust. Consider how practical help changes the conditions another person faces.

passages.title: The request at the threshing floor
passages.summary: Naomi proposes a plan. Ruth approaches Boaz at night and asks for his protection. He promises action after consulting a nearer relative. Ruth asks Boaz to act as a family protector. He promises to settle the matter with the closer relative.
passages.uncertainty: The map shows the named town and broad region. It does not identify private buildings or an ancient road.

lds.text: The older Church manual reads Ruth's action as a request for marriage.

passages.title: The gate agreement and Obed’s birth
passages.summary: Boaz meets the nearer relative and witnesses at the town gate. He marries Ruth. Their son Obed becomes David’s grandfather. The witnesses confirm Boaz’s duty toward Ruth and the family’s land. Naomi’s household gains a future.
passages.uncertainty: The map shows the named town and broad region. It does not identify private buildings or an ancient road.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me compares Boaz’s care with Jesus Christ’s power to redeem, or save. How does Boaz help Ruth and Naomi?
